title: Preventing bedsores in a bedridden person
what: Bedsores are skin wounds caused by long pressure when a person lies or sits without moving. It is easier to prevent them than to treat them.
why: When a person lies in bed or sits in a wheelchair for a long time and can barely change position alone.
duration: ongoing: change position about every 2 hours and check the skin every day
tell_doctor: If red patches appear on the skin that do not fade when pressed
If blisters, sores, or darkening of the skin appear
If the person eats and drinks little or is losing weight
If there is loss of bladder or bowel control

prepare.title: Mattress
prepare.text: An anti-bedsore (pressure-relief) mattress is usually advised. Ask your doctor or nurse which one suits.

prepare.title: Schedule
prepare.text: Make a turning chart and mark every turn.

prepare.title: Bed
prepare.text: Keep the sheet smooth, without wrinkles or crumbs.

prepare.title: Supplies
prepare.text: Pillows and rolls under the knees and heels, and between the legs.

steps: Change the person's position about every 2 hours: back, one side, the other side
Place a pillow between the knees and behind the back when on the side
Keep the heels off the bed, with a roll under the calves
Check the skin every day on the tailbone, heels, shoulder blades, back of the head, and hips
Wash the skin gently and pat dry, do not rub
Change wet bedding and pads right away
feel: Turning may be uncomfortable for the person, so move slowly and explain
Early redness is easy to miss, so look carefully
after: Make sure the person drinks and eats enough
If possible, help them move on their own
Tell your doctor about any new sore
red_flags: An open sore, blister, or black patch on the skin: see a doctor
A wound with pus, a smell, and a fever: see a doctor urgently

faq.a: It is usually not advised, since the ring itself presses on the skin. An anti-bedsore mattress and changing position are better.

faq.q: Can I put iodine-type dye or alcohol on the redness?
faq.a: No, alcohol dries the skin. Show the redness to a doctor or nurse.

reminders.text: Time to turn the person onto the other side and check the skin.
